newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares edge lower at close, Telecom eases again.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares edge lower at close, Telecom eases again.

text.p: * New Zealand shares edge lower at close
* Index mostly affected by continued Telecom weakness
* Telecom, Fletcher Paper actively traded
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
335 -2 * NZSC cap index +7.39 at 5,113.67
374 -1 * Volume NZ$40 million. Futures untraded
732 -5 * Other movers - -7 +25
New Zealand shares edged lower at the close of business on Monday, led mostly by continued weakness in Telecom.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 8.80 points lower at 2,377.94 on turnover worth NZ$40 million.
Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said it was a pedestrian performance given strength in the debt markets, but that turnover was reasonable for a Monday.
Telecom, which ended five cents down at NZ$7.32, accounted for about a quarter of the total turnover.

Koller said Telecom had come under pressure due to concerns that earnings may not be as good as first thought, the threat of cut-price calls through the Internet and litigation brought by BellSouth over alleged bundling of services.
Weakness prevailed throughout most of the session and a bout of late selling, which saw Telecom end on its lows, took the index a little further down.
Lion Nathan eased one cent to NZ$3.74 on light volume as takeover talk surrounding the stock dissipated.
Cultus Petroleum was again very strong, closing 25 cents higher at NZ$2.25, another record high.
Among the stocks to go ex-dividend, DB Group ended two cents down at NZ$1.00 and National Mutual lost seven cents to NZ$1.90. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
